question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Gauge
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Measure.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gauge" (as a verb) means to measure the amount, size or extent of something; as a noun it is an instrument for measuring (e.g., a rain gauge, a fuel gauge). Its closest synonym is therefore "Measure". (मापना / नापने का यंत्र)

◦ Example: The engineer used a special instrument to gauge (measure) the thickness of the steel plate.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Diagnose" means to identify the nature of an illness or a fault (रोग की पहचान करना) — it is about identifying, not measuring.

• Option 2 "Valve" is a device that controls the flow of a liquid or gas (वाल्व) — a noun with no connection to measuring.

• Option 3 "Attempt" means to try to do something (प्रयास करना) — unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of gauge: measure, assess, evaluate, estimate, judge, calculate.

• Common collocations: "gauge the mood of the crowd", "gauge public opinion", "a pressure gauge", "a broad-gauge railway line".

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

The last time he repeated / the same mistake I thought he would / feel many sorry but I was wrong.
option_2: feel many sorry but I was wrong.
option_3: the same mistake I thought he would
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. feel many sorry but I was wrong.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Many" is a quantifier used with plural countable nouns (many books, many people). It can never modify an adjective. Here the adjective "sorry" needs an adverb of degree such as "very / really / extremely".

◦ Correct: The last time he repeated the same mistake I thought he would feel very sorry but I was wrong.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "The last time he repeated" is correct — "the last time" works as a conjunction of time with the simple past.

• Option 3 "the same mistake I thought he would" is correct — "would" is the past form of "will" used in reported/backshifted thought.

• Option 4 "No error" is wrong because the error in "feel many sorry" is clear.

NOTE

• Degree words with adjectives: very, so, quite, rather, extremely, too.

• Quantifiers: many + plural countable (many students), much + uncountable (much water), a lot of + both. Never use "many/much" directly before an adjective.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the bracketed idiom in the given sentence.

The first sample of ore from the trial boring is very promising, but we should remember that (one swallow does not make a summer.)
option_1: The fact of failure or escape is not affected by the narrowness of the margin
option_2: To come out of one trouble and get into a worse
option_3: A single fortunate event does not mean that what follows will also be good.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. A single fortunate event does not mean that what follows will also be good.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The proverb "One swallow does not make a summer" means that one single piece of good luck or one favourable sign does not guarantee that the whole outcome will be good. (एक अकेली अच्छी घटना से पूरा परिणाम अच्छा नहीं हो जाता)

◦ The swallow is a migratory bird whose arrival hints at summer, but the sighting of just one bird is not proof that summer has arrived.

◦ In the sentence, one promising ore sample from a trial boring is not proof that the whole mine will be rich — exactly the sense of the proverb.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 describes the idiom "a miss is as good as a mile" (a narrow escape is still an escape; a narrow failure is still a failure).

• Option 2 describes "out of the frying pan into the fire" (आग से निकलकर कड़ाही में).

• Option 4 loosely describes "lock, stock and barrel" (the whole of something).

NOTE

• Related proverbs of caution: "Don't count your chickens before they hatch", "All that glitters is not gold", "Rome was not built in a day".

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

I rode my bike to worked those morning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. work this.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Two corrections are needed in the underlined part "worked those":

◦ After the preposition "to" (here "to work" = the infinitive showing purpose — I rode my bike to work), the base form/noun "work" is required, not the past form "worked".

◦ The time expression is the singular noun "morning", so the singular demonstrative "this" must be used, not the plural "those".

◦ Correct: I rode my bike to work this morning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "worked this" keeps the wrong verb form "worked".

• Option 2 "work these" wrongly uses the plural "these" with the singular "morning".

• Option 3 "No improvement" is wrong because the sentence as printed is clearly ungrammatical.

NOTE

• Demonstratives: this/that with singular nouns (this morning, that boy); these/those with plural nouns (these mornings, those boys).

• "Go/ride/drive to work" is a fixed expression in which "work" is an uncountable noun (no article).

question: Select the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Epiphany.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Epiphany", which means a sudden, striking realisation or moment of insight; with a capital E it is also the Christian festival (6 January) marking the manifestation of Christ to the Magi. (अचानक होने वाला ज्ञानोदय / बोध)

◦ Spelling key: E + PI + PHA + NY.

◦ Example: While walking home, she had an epiphany about how to solve the problem.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Epephany", "Epiphene" and "Epipheny" are all misspellings — the word takes "-pha-" in the middle and ends in "-ny".

NOTE

• Words of similar formation from Greek "phainein" (to show): epiphany, phenomenon, phantom, diaphanous.

• Synonyms of epiphany: revelation, insight, realisation, illumination, eye-opener.

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym to substitute the bracketed word in the given sentence.

So it would appear that from now on I am going to have to be more (tactful) and diplomatic in my meanderings.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Ungracious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Tactful" means showing skill and sensitivity in dealing with others; careful not to offend. (व्यवहार-कुशल)

• Its antonym is "Ungracious", meaning rude, discourteous and lacking in politeness or grace. (अशिष्ट / रूखा)

◦ Example: His ungracious refusal embarrassed everyone at the table.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Sycophantic" means flattering someone in a servile way (चापलूस) — not the opposite of tactful.

• Option 2 "Fawning" means seeking favour by excessive flattery (खुशामद करना) — again a form of flattery, not rudeness.

• Option 3 "Grovelling" means behaving in an abjectly humble way (गिड़गिड़ाना) — not an antonym of tactful.

NOTE

• Synonyms of tactful: diplomatic, discreet, considerate, sensitive, politic.

• Antonyms of tactful: tactless, blunt, indiscreet, ungracious, rude.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

The timescale of prokaryote evolution / have been difficult to reconstruct / because of a limited fossil record.
option_1: because of a limited fossil record.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. have been difficult to reconstruct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "The timescale", which is singular. The phrase "of prokaryote evolution" is only a prepositional phrase and does not change the number of the subject.

• Therefore the verb must be the singular "has been", not the plural "have been".

◦ Correct: The timescale of prokaryote evolution has been difficult to reconstruct because of a limited fossil record.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "because of a limited fossil record." is correct — "because of" is followed by a noun phrase.

• Option 2 "The timescale of prokaryote evolution" is a correct noun phrase.

• Option 4 "No error" is wrong since the subject–verb agreement is clearly faulty.

NOTE

• Rule (Subject–Verb Agreement): the verb agrees with the head noun of the subject, not with the noun in the intervening "of" phrase.

◦ The quality of the mangoes is poor. / The list of candidates has been published.

• "Because of" (preposition + noun) vs "because" (conjunction + clause).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Join our networks to ______ better Governance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. promote.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Promote" means to support actively, encourage or further the progress of something. Joining a network in order to promote better governance makes complete sense. (बढ़ावा देना)

◦ Correct: Join our networks to promote better Governance.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "drain" means to empty out or exhaust (सोख लेना) — the opposite of the positive sense required.

• Option 2 "disintegrate" means to break into pieces (टुकड़े-टुकड़े होना) — negative and illogical here.

• Option 4 "sedate" means to calm someone with a drug (शांत करना / नशीली दवा देना) — completely out of context.

NOTE

• Synonyms of promote: encourage, foster, further, advance, boost, advocate.

• "Promote" also means to raise someone to a higher rank ("He was promoted to manager") and to advertise a product ("promote a new phone").

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Participants in our studies reviewed these online dating profiles.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Participants in our studies reviewed these online dating profiles." is completely correct:

◦ Subject: "Participants" (plural) — verb "reviewed" (simple past, same for all persons and numbers). ✔

◦ "in our studies" is a correctly formed prepositional phrase modifying "Participants". ✔

◦ "these online dating profiles" — the plural demonstrative "these" correctly matches the plural noun "profiles". ✔

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Since no segment contains a grammatical, spelling or usage error, the answer must be "No error".

NOTE

• In such SSC "spot the error" questions, always check in order: subject–verb agreement, tense, articles, prepositions, pronoun–antecedent agreement, and parallelism. If all check out, "No error" is the answer — it is a genuine option and is correct in roughly one out of every few questions.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

Persons who are unfairly blamed for something that others have done
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Scapegoat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "scapegoat" is a person who is blamed for the wrongdoings or mistakes of others. (बलि का बकरा)

◦ Example: The junior clerk was made a scapegoat for the department's failure.

◦ The word comes from an ancient ritual in which a goat was symbolically loaded with the sins of the people and driven into the wilderness.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Expedition" means a journey undertaken for a specific purpose (अभियान).

• Option 2 "Epitome" means a perfect example or embodiment of something (सार / प्रतिरूप).

• Option 3 "Disdain" means contempt or scorn (तिरस्कार).

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: scapegoat (one blamed for others' faults), culprit (the actual offender), accomplice (a partner in crime), martyr (one who suffers for a cause).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Multi-client messaging systems make it easier to keep in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. touch.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiomatic phrase "keep in touch (with someone)" means to remain in regular communication or contact. Messaging systems obviously help people stay in contact. (संपर्क में रहना)

◦ Correct: Multi-client messaging systems make it easier to keep in touch.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "keep in diary" is not an English collocation (one "keeps a diary").

• Option 3 "keep in roll" is not standard ("keep on the rolls" exists in an administrative sense only).

• Option 4 "keep in secret" is wrong — the correct expression is "keep something secret" or "keep it a secret".

NOTE

• Useful "touch" expressions: keep/stay in touch (remain in contact), lose touch (stop communicating), get in touch (make contact), out of touch (no longer informed or in contact).

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

I ______ the cake before my mother arrived.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. had baked.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When two actions happen in the past, the action that happened earlier is put in the past perfect (had + V3) and the later one in the simple past.

◦ Here, the baking happened before the mother arrived, so: "I had baked the cake before my mother arrived."

• The conjunction "before" is a strong signal for the past perfect in the main clause.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "bake" (simple present) does not match the past-time context of "arrived".

• Option 3 "baked" (simple past) is grammatically possible in loose speech but does not bring out the "earlier action" relation the question tests.

• Option 4 "have baked" (present perfect) cannot be used with a definite past time reference such as "before my mother arrived".

NOTE

• Past perfect = had + past participle (V3), used for the earlier of two past events: "The train had left before we reached the station."

• Present perfect (have/has + V3) is never used with a finished past time expression (yesterday, last year, in 1990).

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

Bearing no name
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Anonymous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Anonymous" means bearing no name; of unknown name or authorship. (नामरहित / गुमनाम)

◦ Example: The police received an anonymous letter naming the thief.

◦ Etymology: Greek "an-" (without) + "onyma" (name).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Namesake" is a person having the same name as another (हमनाम) — the opposite idea.

• Option 3 "Anomaly" means something that deviates from the normal or expected (असंगति).

• Option 4 "Pseudonym" is a false name adopted by an author (छद्म नाम) — a pen name is still a name, so it is not "bearing no name".

NOTE

• Related "-onym" words: synonym (same meaning), antonym (opposite meaning), homonym (same sound/spelling), acronym (word formed from initials), eponym (a name that gives its name to something).

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Disregard
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Curiosity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Disregard" means to pay no attention to; to ignore or take no notice of something. (उपेक्षा करना / ध्यान न देना)

• Its opposite among the given choices is "Curiosity", which is a strong desire to know or learn — i.e., active interest and attention, the very opposite of ignoring something. (जिज्ञासा)

◦ Example: He disregarded the warning signs, while his friend examined them with great curiosity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Hidden" means concealed (छिपा हुआ) — unrelated to attention or neglect.

• Option 3 "Demote" means to lower someone in rank (पदावनत करना) — unrelated.

• Option 4 "Split" means to divide or break apart (विभाजित करना) — unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of disregard: ignore, overlook, neglect, brush aside, pay no heed to.

• Antonyms of disregard: regard, heed, attention, notice, interest, curiosity, consideration.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Eventually, the water will ______ through the surrounding concrete.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. permeate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Permeate" means to spread through and be absorbed by something; to pass through a porous substance. Water passing through concrete is exactly "permeating". (रिसकर फैल जाना / व्याप्त होना)

◦ Correct: Eventually, the water will permeate through the surrounding concrete.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "statolith" is a noun (a tiny gravity-sensing body in plants and some animals) — a noun cannot follow "will".

• Option 2 "aerate" means to introduce air into a liquid or soil (हवा मिलाना) — it does not describe seeping through.

• Option 4 "delegate" means to entrust a task to someone else (कार्यभार सौंपना) — completely out of context.

NOTE

• Synonyms of permeate: penetrate, seep through, soak through, pervade, infuse, saturate.

• The related adjective is "permeable" (allowing liquids to pass through) and its opposite "impermeable" — an important term in geography (permeable rocks such as sandstone vs impermeable rocks such as granite).

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

She ran 12 kms at a stretch, (which are a greater) distance for a rookie.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. which is quite some.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The relative pronoun refers to the singular noun "distance", so the singular verb "is" is needed, not "are".

• The comparative "greater" is wrong because no comparison with "than" is made in the sentence. The idiomatic expression "quite some distance" means a considerable/impressive distance, which fits the admiring tone about a rookie runner.

◦ Correct: She ran 12 kms at a stretch, which is quite some distance for a rookie.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No correction required" is wrong — "which are a greater" is both ungrammatical (plural verb) and unidiomatic.

• Option 3 "which are greatest" keeps the plural verb error and adds a superlative without "the".

• Option 4 "what is great" is wrong — the relative pronoun "what" cannot introduce a relative clause referring back to a stated noun; "which" is required.

NOTE

• "Quite some" before a noun = a large or impressive amount ("quite some time", "quite some distance", "quite some achievement").

• A comparative degree ("greater") normally needs a point of comparison introduced by "than".

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To meet one's eyes
option_1: To look at someone directly while they are looking at you
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To look at someone directly while they are looking at you.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to meet one's eyes" (also "to meet someone's eye/gaze") means to look directly at a person at the same moment that they are looking at you — to make eye contact. (आँखें मिलाना)

◦ Example: He was so ashamed that he could not meet her eyes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "To confess something" corresponds to idioms like "to come clean / to make a clean breast of".

• Option 3 "To make haste" corresponds to "to hurry up / to get a move on".

• Option 4 "To meet someone regularly" is a literal, non-idiomatic meaning and is not what the phrase conveys.

NOTE

• Related "eye" idioms: see eye to eye (agree completely), turn a blind eye (ignore deliberately), keep an eye on (watch carefully), an eye for an eye (revenge), in the public eye (well known).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

This preoccupation with him was becoming an obsession (that was beginning to effect her) ability to take care of the house.
option_1: that was beginning to affect her ability
option_2: which was beginning to effect her ability
option_4: which was begin to affect her ability
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. that was beginning to affect her ability.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The required word is the verb "affect" (to influence / to have an impact on), not the noun "effect" (a result). Since it follows "beginning to", a verb is needed.

◦ Correct: ... an obsession that was beginning to affect her ability to take care of the house.

• The relative pronoun "that" correctly introduces the defining clause describing "obsession".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 retains the wrong word "effect" (noun) in a verb slot.

• Option 3 "No substitution required" is wrong because the printed sentence has the affect/effect error.

• Option 4 "which was begin to affect" is doubly wrong — "was begin" is not a valid verb form (it should be "was beginning").

NOTE

• Affect (verb) = to influence: "Smoking affects your health." (प्रभावित करना)

• Effect (noun) = result/consequence: "Smoking has a bad effect on health." (प्रभाव)

• "Effect" can rarely be a formal verb meaning "to bring about" — "to effect a change".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Equivocal
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Ambiguous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Equivocal" means open to more than one interpretation; deliberately vague or unclear. Its closest synonym is "Ambiguous". (अस्पष्ट / द्व्यर्थक)

◦ Example: The minister gave an equivocal (ambiguous) reply that satisfied neither side.

◦ Etymology: Latin "aequus" (equal) + "vocare" (to call) — literally "of equal voices", i.e., two meanings of equal weight.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Definite" (clear and certain) is a direct antonym.

• Option 2 "Secure" (safe, protected) and Option 3 "Insecure" (unsafe, lacking confidence) belong to a different field of meaning altogether.

NOTE

• Synonyms of equivocal: ambiguous, vague, evasive, obscure, cryptic, indeterminate.

• Antonyms: unequivocal, unambiguous, clear, definite, explicit.

question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: Everything hurrt in a dull, constant way.
option_2: Everything hurt in a dul, contant weigh.
option_3: Everything hurt in a dull, contsant way.
option_4: Everything hurt in a dull, constant way.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Everything hurt in a dull, constant way.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Every word in Option 4 is spelt correctly: "hurt", "dull", "constant" and "way".

◦ Correct: Everything hurt in a dull, constant way.

• "Hurt" is an irregular verb whose forms are all the same: hurt – hurt – hurt (no double "r").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 misspells "hurt" as "hurrt".

• Option 2 misspells "dull" as "dul" and "constant" as "contant", and wrongly uses the homophone "weigh" (to measure weight) in place of "way" (manner).

• Option 3 misspells "constant" as "contsant" (transposed letters).

NOTE

• Homophones to remember: way / weigh / whey, their / there / they're, principal / principle, stationary / stationery.

• Spelling key: CON + STANT; DULL takes a double "l".

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

The “Sesame Street” spinoff (1) ______ to be the first Russian-language educational TV (2) ______ aimed specifically at preschoolers. The project (3) ______ support from both American and Russian government officials. “If we do not reform our (4) ______, we can hardly hope that we will reform our society,” (5) ______ Elena Lenskaya, a director in Russia’s Ministry of Education, during a 1992 U.S. congressional hearing on the planned adaptation.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. set out.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "set out (to do something)" means to begin a task with a particular aim or intention. The spinoff set out to be the first Russian-language educational TV programme for preschoolers. (किसी उद्देश्य से शुरुआत करना)

◦ Correct: The "Sesame Street" spinoff set out to be the first Russian-language educational TV programme ...

• Only "set out" takes a to-infinitive ("set out to be / set out to prove") in this sense.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "set in" means to begin and be likely to continue, used of bad weather or unpleasant conditions ("The rains have set in").

• Option 3 "set off" means to start a journey or to cause something to explode/begin ("They set off at dawn"; "The spark set off an explosion").

• Option 4 "set aside" means to keep something for a special purpose or to annul a judgement ("set aside some money"; "the court set aside the order").

NOTE

• More "set" phrasal verbs: set up (establish), set about (start doing), set back (delay), set down (write/record), set forth (state clearly).

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

The “Sesame Street” spinoff (1) ______ to be the first Russian-language educational TV (2) ______ aimed specifically at preschoolers. The project (3) ______ support from both American and Russian government officials. “If we do not reform our (4) ______, we can hardly hope that we will reform our society,” (5) ______ Elena Lenskaya, a director in Russia’s Ministry of Education, during a 1992 U.S. congressional hearing on the planned adaptation.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. program.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A television broadcast is called a "programme/program". The phrase "educational TV program aimed specifically at preschoolers" is the natural collocation. (कार्यक्रम)

◦ Correct: ... the first Russian-language educational TV program aimed specifically at preschoolers.

• The passage uses American spelling ("program"), consistent with the American origin of "Sesame Street".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "solution" (an answer to a problem) cannot be "aimed at preschoolers" in a TV context.

• Option 3 "pattern" (a design or a regular arrangement) does not collocate with "TV".

• Option 4 "recipe" (instructions for cooking) is completely out of context.

NOTE

• "TV programme" (British) / "TV program" (American). Both are correct; SSC papers accept the spelling used in the passage.

• "Sesame Street" is a famous American children's educational television series that has been adapted in many countries (in India as "Galli Galli Sim Sim").

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

The “Sesame Street” spinoff (1) ______ to be the first Russian-language educational TV (2) ______ aimed specifically at preschoolers. The project (3) ______ support from both American and Russian government officials. “If we do not reform our (4) ______, we can hardly hope that we will reform our society,” (5) ______ Elena Lenskaya, a director in Russia’s Ministry of Education, during a 1992 U.S. congressional hearing on the planned adaptation.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. received.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage narrates past events (the 1992 hearing), so the simple past tense "received" is required as the main verb of the clause "The project received support from both American and Russian government officials."

◦ Correct: The project received support from both American and Russian government officials.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "did received" is wrong — after the auxiliary "did" the base form is used ("did receive"), never the past form.

• Option 3 "receiving" is a participle and cannot stand alone as the finite verb of the clause (it would need "was/were receiving").

• Option 4 "receive" (present) does not agree with the past-time narrative and also disagrees with the singular subject in the present tense (it would need "receives").

NOTE

• Emphatic "do/does/did" is always followed by V1: "He did receive the letter."

• Simple past (V2) is used for a completed action at a definite past time.

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

The “Sesame Street” spinoff (1) ______ to be the first Russian-language educational TV (2) ______ aimed specifically at preschoolers. The project (3) ______ support from both American and Russian government officials. “If we do not reform our (4) ______, we can hardly hope that we will reform our society,” (5) ______ Elena Lenskaya, a director in Russia’s Ministry of Education, during a 1992 U.S. congressional hearing on the planned adaptation.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. education.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The words are spoken by "Elena Lenskaya, a director in Russia's Ministry of Education", and the whole passage is about an educational television programme. The quotation contrasts two different things — "if we do not reform our education, we can hardly hope that we will reform our society".

◦ Correct: "If we do not reform our education, we can hardly hope that we will reform our society."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "society" cannot be used, because "society" already appears in the second half of the same sentence; repeating it would destroy the contrast the speaker is making.

• Option 2 "politics" and Option 4 "economy" are not the subject of the passage, which is about children's educational television.

NOTE

• In cloze (fill-in-the-blank) passages, always use contextual clues — here the speaker's designation ("Ministry of Education") and the logical contrast within the sentence point straight to the answer.

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

The “Sesame Street” spinoff (1) ______ to be the first Russian-language educational TV (2) ______ aimed specifically at preschoolers. The project (3) ______ support from both American and Russian government officials. “If we do not reform our (4) ______, we can hardly hope that we will reform our society,” (5) ______ Elena Lenskaya, a director in Russia’s Ministry of Education, during a 1992 U.S. congressional hearing on the planned adaptation.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. said.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank comes immediately after a direct quotation and before the speaker's name. The standard reporting verb in this position is "said".

◦ Correct: "... we will reform our society," said Elena Lenskaya, a director in Russia's Ministry of Education ...

• "Said" is used without an indirect object (said + something / said to someone), which is exactly what is needed here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "told" always requires a direct object (a person) — "told us", "told the committee". "Told Elena Lenskaya" would wrongly make her the listener, not the speaker.

• Option 2 "ordered" would mean she gave a command, which does not match a reflective statement at a hearing.

• Option 4 "muted" means to make a sound softer or to silence something — it is not a reporting verb.

NOTE

• Say vs Tell: "say something (to somebody)" but "tell somebody something". "He said that he was tired." / "He told me that he was tired."

• Inversion after a quotation ("said Elena Lenskaya") is normal in reported speech in journalism.

question: What is the chemical name of Marble?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calcium carbonate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Marble is a metamorphic rock whose chemical name is "Calcium carbonate", with the formula CaCO₃. (संगमरमर — कैल्शियम कार्बोनेट)

• It is formed by the metamorphism of limestone under heat and pressure; limestone too is chemically CaCO₃.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other common compounds: Magnesium oxide (MgO) — used in antacids and refractories; Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) — caustic soda; Calcium hydroxide [Ca(OH)₂] — slaked lime, used in whitewashing.

• Other natural forms of CaCO₃: limestone, chalk, calcite, and the shells of molluscs.

NOTE

• The Taj Mahal at Agra is built of white Makrana marble from Rajasthan.

• Marble reacts with dilute acids releasing CO₂, which is why acid rain damages marble monuments (a phenomenon called "marble cancer").

question: Kodon, Kutki, Hraka, Bauti are examples of __________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is millets.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kodon (Kodo), Kutki (little millet), Hraka and Bauti" are traditional varieties of "millets" — coarse, hardy cereal grains grown mainly in dry, rain-fed regions of India. (मोटे अनाज / श्री अन्न)

• They are highly nutritious, rich in fibre, iron and calcium, and need very little water.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Major millets in India: Jowar (sorghum), Bajra (pearl millet), Ragi (finger millet); minor millets: Kodo, Kutki (little millet), Kangni (foxtail), Sanwa (barnyard), Cheena (proso).

• India is the largest producer of millets in the world, with Rajasthan, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh among the leading states.

NOTE

• On India's proposal, the United Nations declared 2023 as the International Year of Millets. The Government of India has rebranded millets as "Shree Anna".

question: As per census 2011, what was the percentage of urban population in India? (Provide an approximate range)
solution_text:
The correct answer is 30-35%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, about 31.16% (roughly 31%) of India's population lived in urban areas — i.e., in the range of "30-35%". (शहरी जनसंख्या — लगभग 31%)

• The remaining 68.84% lived in rural areas.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Census 2011 was the 15th National Census of India and the 7th after Independence; its slogan was "Our Census, Our Future".

• Total population in 2011: 1,210.9 million (121 crore); decadal growth 17.7%; sex ratio 943; literacy rate 74.04%; density 382 persons per sq km.

• Most urbanised states/UTs: Delhi, Goa, Mizoram and Tamil Nadu; least urbanised: Himachal Pradesh and Bihar.

NOTE

• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years under the Census Act, 1948, by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (Ministry of Home Affairs). The first synchronous census was held in 1881 under Lord Ripon.

question: Where were the 5th edition of the Khelo India Youth Games held in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 5th edition of the Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG) 2022, held from 30 January to 11 February 2023, was hosted by "Madhya Pradesh", with Bhopal, Indore, Gwalior, Jabalpur, Ujjain and Balaghat as venues. (खेलो इंडिया यूथ गेम्स — मध्य प्रदेश)

• Maharashtra topped the medal tally at these Games.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Khelo India programme was launched in 2018 by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to revive sports culture and identify talent at the grassroots.

• Editions: 2018 – New Delhi, 2019 – Pune (Maharashtra), 2020 – Guwahati (Assam), 2021/22 – Panchkula (Haryana), 2022/23 – Madhya Pradesh, 2023 – Tamil Nadu.

• The mascot of the Madhya Pradesh edition was "Ashtalakshmi" (based on the state's barasingha/swamp deer theme).

NOTE

• Other Khelo India events: Khelo India University Games, Khelo India Winter Games and Khelo India Para Games.

question: Babur defeated Mahmud Lodi and Sultan Nusrat Shah thus establishing Mughal rule in India in the Battle of _______ in 1529.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghagra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Battle of Ghagra (Ghaghra), 1529, Babur defeated the combined Afghan forces of Mahmud Lodi and Sultan Nusrat Shah of Bengal, thereby consolidating Mughal rule in India. (घाघरा का युद्ध — 1529)

• It was Babur's last major battle; he died in 1530.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Babur's key battles: First Battle of Panipat (1526) against Ibrahim Lodi; Battle of Khanwa (1527) against Rana Sanga; Battle of Chanderi (1528) against Medini Rai; Battle of Ghagra (1529) against the Afghans.

• Chausa (1539) and Kannauj/Bilgram (1540) were battles in which Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun.

NOTE

• Babur wrote his memoirs, the "Tuzuk-i-Baburi (Baburnama)", in Turki. He introduced the Tulughma war tactic and the effective use of field artillery in India.

question: Which RBI tool refers to buying and selling of bonds issued by the Government in the open market?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Open Market Operations.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Open Market Operations (OMO)" refer to the purchase and sale of government securities (bonds) by the RBI in the open market to manage the money supply and liquidity in the economy. (खुले बाज़ार की क्रियाएँ)

◦ Buying securities injects liquidity (increases money supply); selling securities absorbs liquidity (reduces money supply).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) allows banks to borrow through repo and park funds through reverse repo with the RBI.

• Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) lets banks borrow overnight from the RBI against their SLR securities, at a rate above the repo rate.

• Moral suasion is a qualitative (persuasive) tool — the RBI advises or persuades banks, without any legal compulsion.

NOTE

• Quantitative tools of the RBI: Bank Rate, Repo & Reverse Repo, CRR, SLR, OMO, MSF.

• Qualitative tools: margin requirements, moral suasion, credit rationing, direct action, consumer credit regulation.

• The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 and nationalised in 1949.

question: Who among the following was known as the 'Queen of Thumri'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Girija Devi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Girija Devi (1929–2017) of the Banaras (Seniya and Banaras) gharana was popularly known as the "Queen of Thumri" (Thumri Queen) for her mastery of the semi-classical form. (ठुमरी की रानी — गिरिजा देवी)

• She popularised thumri, tappa, kajri, chaiti and hori and was honoured with the Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan, and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Siddheswari Devi was also a great Banaras thumri singer and Girija Devi's contemporary.

• Gangubai Hangal was a famous Kirana gharana khayal singer from Karnataka.

• Begum Parveen Sultana is a celebrated Patiala gharana vocalist from Assam.

NOTE

• Thumri is a semi-classical (light classical) vocal form of Hindustani music, romantic and devotional in mood, usually sung in ragas like Khamaj, Pilu, Kafi and Bhairavi.

question: After which war, Ashoka abandoned the policy of physical occupation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalinga War.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the Kalinga War (c. 261 BCE), the Mauryan emperor Ashoka was so shaken by the bloodshed that he gave up the policy of conquest by war (Bherighosha) and adopted the policy of conquest by dhamma (Dhammaghosha). (कलिंग युद्ध — अशोक)

• The war is described in Ashoka's Rock Edict XIII (Major Rock Edict 13), which records about 100,000 killed, 150,000 deported and many more who died.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Battle of the Hydaspes (326 BCE) was fought between Alexander and Porus on the river Jhelum.

• Battles of Tarain (1191 and 1192) were fought between Prithviraj Chauhan and Muhammad Ghori.

• After Kalinga, Ashoka embraced Buddhism (influenced by the monk Upagupta) and sent his children Mahendra and Sanghamitra to Sri Lanka to spread the faith.

NOTE

• Ashoka's edicts were deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837. Ashoka is called "Devanampiya Piyadassi" in his inscriptions. India's national emblem is adapted from his Sarnath Lion Capital.

question: Which among the following planets is also known as Earth's twin?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Venus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Venus" is called Earth's twin (sister planet) because it is almost the same size, mass and density as Earth and is our nearest planetary neighbour. (पृथ्वी का जुड़वाँ ग्रह — शुक्र)

• Venus is also the brightest planet in the sky and is known as the "morning star" and "evening star".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Venus is the hottest planet (about 462 °C) because of a runaway greenhouse effect caused by its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere.

• Venus and Uranus rotate from east to west (retrograde); on Venus a day is longer than its year (rotation ≈ 243 Earth days, revolution ≈ 225 Earth days).

• Venus has no moon and no satellite, like Mercury.

NOTE

• Nicknames: Mercury — swiftest planet; Mars — Red Planet; Jupiter — largest planet; Saturn — ringed planet; Uranus — green planet; Neptune — blue planet.

question: Which among the following chemicals is used to purify water as a disinfectant?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chlorine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Chlorine" is the chemical most widely used to disinfect drinking water; it kills bacteria and other pathogens. The process is called "chlorination". (जल का क्लोरीनीकरण)

• At home, water is disinfected with bleaching powder (calcium hypochlorite) or chlorine tablets.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Ethanol is used as an antiseptic on skin and in sanitisers, not for treating drinking-water supplies.

• Phosphor is a substance that emits light (used in fluorescent tubes and TV screens).

• Teflon (PTFE) is a non-stick polymer used to coat cookware.

NOTE

• Other water purification methods: boiling, filtration, UV treatment, ozonisation, reverse osmosis and use of alum (potash alum) for coagulation.

• Chlorine (Cl) has atomic number 17 and belongs to Group 17 (halogens).

question: Who was the spiritual guru of Swami Vivekananda?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ramakrishna Paramahansa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ramakrishna Paramahansa (1836–1886)", the saint of the Dakshineswar Kali Temple in Bengal, was the spiritual guru of Swami Vivekananda. (स्वामी विवेकानंद के गुरु — रामकृष्ण परमहंस)

• He taught that all religions lead to the same God ("Jato mat, tato path" — as many faiths, so many paths).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Narendra Dutta (Narendranath Datta)" was the original name of Swami Vivekananda himself, so Option 1 is a distractor.

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale was the political guru of Mahatma Gandhi; Acharya Narendra Dev was a socialist leader.

• Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 at Belur (near Kolkata) and delivered his famous address at the World Parliament of Religions, Chicago, on 11 September 1893.

NOTE

• National Youth Day is celebrated on 12 January, the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda. His notable works include "Raja Yoga", "Karma Yoga" and "Jnana Yoga".

question: Who among the following won the Sultan of Johor Cup 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "India" won the Sultan of Johor Cup 2022, defeating Australia 5-4 in the final at Johor Bahru, Malaysia. (सुल्तान ऑफ जोहोर कप 2022 — भारत)

• It was India's second title in this tournament (the first was in 2013).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Sultan of Johor Cup is an annual under-21 (junior) men's hockey tournament held in Johor Bahru, Malaysia, since 2011.

• Malaysia also hosts the Sultan Azlan Shah Cup, a senior men's invitational hockey tournament held at Ipoh.

NOTE

• Major hockey events: Hockey World Cup, Olympic hockey, FIH Pro League, Asian Games, Azlan Shah Cup, Sultan of Johor Cup.

• India won hockey gold at the Olympics 8 times and took the bronze at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024.

question: Agra Fort is one of the popular Mughal monuments built in the 16th century by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Akbar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Agra Fort" (the Red Fort of Agra) was built by the Mughal emperor "Akbar" from 1565 to 1573 on the bank of the Yamuna, mainly of red sandstone. (आगरा का किला — अकबर)

• It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Structures inside the fort: Jahangiri Mahal (Akbar's construction), and Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas, Moti Masjid, Khas Mahal, Sheesh Mahal and Musamman Burj (mostly built by Shah Jahan in white marble).

• Shah Jahan was imprisoned in the Musamman Burj of this fort by his son Aurangzeb, from where he could see the Taj Mahal.

NOTE

• Other Akbar-era monuments: Fatehpur Sikri, Buland Darwaza, Ibadat Khana, Humayun's Tomb (built under his reign by Bega Begum) and the Lahore and Allahabad forts.

question: Which among the following dance forms was originally performed in the temples of Tamil Nadu, by the Devadasis and therefore it is also known as Dasiattam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatnatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bharatnatyam" is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, originally performed in temples by the Devadasis, which is why it was also called "Dasiattam (Sadir/Dasi Attam)". (भरतनाट्यम — दासीअट्टम)

• It is based on the "Natya Shastra" of Bharata Muni and is often called the "fire dance" for its geometric, fire-like postures.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Its revival in the 20th century is credited to Rukmini Devi Arundale (founder of Kalakshetra) and E. Krishna Iyer.

• Famous exponents: Rukmini Devi Arundale, Balasaraswati, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Padma Subrahmanyam, Mallika Sarabhai.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances and their states: Bharatnatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yojana was launched in _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2000.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yojana (PMGY)" was launched in the year "2000" (in the Union Budget of 2000-01) to focus on the basic minimum needs of rural people. (प्रधानमंत्री ग्रामोदय योजना — 2000)

• It provided Additional Central Assistance to states for primary health, primary education, rural shelter, rural drinking water, nutrition and rural electrification.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The scheme was launched during the tenure of Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

• Its rural roads component, "Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)", also launched in December 2000, is now a major standalone scheme providing all-weather roads to unconnected habitations.

NOTE

• Other rural development schemes: MGNREGA (2005/2006), NRLM–Aajeevika (2011), DDU-GKY (2014), PMAY-Gramin (2016), Sansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (2014).

question: The constituent assembly was formed on the recommendation of the Cabinet Mission which visited India in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1946.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Constituent Assembly of India was constituted in November-December 1946 under the plan of the "Cabinet Mission", which visited India in "1946". (कैबिनेट मिशन — 1946)

• The Cabinet Mission consisted of three British Cabinet members: Pethick-Lawrence (Chairman), Stafford Cripps and A. V. Alexander.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Constituent Assembly held its first sitting on 9 December 1946; Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was the temporary (interim) President and Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected the permanent President on 11 December 1946.

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee (formed 29 August 1947).

• The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950; the Assembly took 2 years, 11 months and 18 days.

NOTE

• The idea of a Constituent Assembly was first put forward by M. N. Roy in 1934; it was officially accepted for the first time in the August Offer (1940) and conceded in the Cripps Mission (1942).

question: The Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2022 aims to regulate mergers and acquisitions based on the value of transactions, and says that deals with transaction value of more than ₹2,000 crore will require the Competition Commission of India's approval. For faster approvals, the proposed law also says the timeline for CCI to pass an order on such transactions will be reduced to ______ days from 210 days.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 150.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2022" proposed reducing the time limit for the Competition Commission of India (CCI) to pass an order on combinations (mergers and acquisitions) from 210 days to "150" days, to speed up approvals. (210 दिन से घटाकर 150 दिन)

• It also introduced a deal-value threshold: transactions worth more than ₹2,000 crore need CCI approval.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Competition Commission of India (CCI) was established in 2003 and became fully functional in 2009, under the Competition Act, 2002, which replaced the MRTP Act, 1969.

• The CCI prohibits anti-competitive agreements, abuse of dominant position, and regulates combinations (mergers, amalgamations, acquisitions).

• The Bill was passed as the Competition (Amendment) Act, 2023.

NOTE

• The Competition Act, 2002 was based on the recommendations of the Raghavan Committee. Appeals against CCI orders lie with the NCLAT, and thereafter with the Supreme Court.

question: Which among the following Acts introduced the Diarchy, i.e., rule of two which means executive councillors and popular ministers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Montague-Chelmsford Reform (Government of India Act), 1919.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms)" introduced "Diarchy (dyarchy) — the rule of two" in the provinces, dividing provincial subjects into:

◦ Transferred subjects — administered by the Governor with the aid of ministers responsible to the legislature (education, health, local self-government, agriculture);

◦ Reserved subjects — administered by the Governor with his executive councillors (police, justice, land revenue, irrigation).

◦ (द्वैध शासन — 1919 का अधिनियम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Act of 1919 also introduced bicameralism and direct elections at the centre, separated central and provincial budgets, and created the office of the High Commissioner for India in London. It provided for a statutory commission after 10 years (which came as the Simon Commission, 1927).

• The Charter Act, 1813 ended the Company's trade monopoly (except tea and trade with China) and allowed missionaries.

• The Government of India Act, 1858 abolished the East India Company and transferred power to the British Crown, creating the Secretary of State for India.

• The Indian Councils Act, 1861 began the portfolio system and associated Indians with law-making.

NOTE

• Diarchy in the provinces was abolished by the Government of India Act, 1935, which instead introduced provincial autonomy and diarchy at the centre (never implemented).

question: A biopic on legendary Sitara Devi has been announced on her 101st birth anniversary by producer Raj C Anand. Sitara Devi was a recognized __________ dancer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sitara Devi (1920–2014) was a legendary Indian "Kathak" dancer, popularly called "Nritya Samragini" (the Empress of Dance) — a title given to her by Rabindranath Tagore. (कथक नृत्यांगना — सितारा देवी)

• She belonged to the Banaras gharana of Kathak and was awarded the Padma Shri (1973) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1969).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh); the name comes from "katha" (story) — the "kathakars" narrated stories through dance.

• Kathak gharanas: Lucknow, Jaipur, Banaras and Raigarh.

• Other famous Kathak exponents: Birju Maharaj, Shambhu Maharaj, Lachhu Maharaj, Damayanti Joshi, Kumudini Lakhia.

NOTE

• Kathak is the only classical dance form with strong Persian and Mughal court influence, marked by fast chakkars (spins), intricate footwork (tatkar) and expressive abhinaya.

question: The Ugadi festival in India celebrates the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is commencement of new year.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ugadi (Yugadi)" marks the "commencement of the new year" as per the lunisolar Hindu calendar. The word comes from "Yuga" (age) + "Adi" (beginning). (उगादि — नववर्ष का आरंभ)

• It is celebrated in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka on the first day of the month of Chaitra (March–April).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A special dish, "Ugadi Pachadi", is prepared with six tastes (sweet, sour, salty, bitter, pungent, astringent), symbolising the different experiences of life.

• The same new year is celebrated as Gudi Padwa in Maharashtra, Cheti Chand by Sindhis, Navreh in Kashmir, Baisakhi in Punjab, Puthandu in Tamil Nadu, Vishu in Kerala, Bihu in Assam and Poila Boishakh in Bengal.

NOTE

• Harvest festivals in India: Pongal, Makar Sankranti, Lohri, Baisakhi, Onam, Nuakhai and Bihu.

question: Balanoglossus belongs to which of the following phylum of animal kingdom?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hemichordata.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Balanoglossus" (the acorn worm or tongue worm) belongs to the phylum "Hemichordata". (हेमीकॉर्डेटा)

• Hemichordates are marine, worm-like animals with a body divided into proboscis, collar and trunk; they have a stomochord (a rudimentary notochord-like structure), gill slits and an open circulatory system.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Arthropoda is the largest phylum of the animal kingdom (insects, spiders, crabs) — jointed legs and a chitinous exoskeleton.

• Echinodermata (starfish, sea urchin) are exclusively marine, with water-vascular systems and spiny skin.

• Mollusca (snail, octopus, Pila) is the second largest phylum, with a soft body usually covered by a calcareous shell.

NOTE

• Hemichordata was earlier placed as a sub-phylum of Chordata, but is now treated as a separate phylum because a true notochord is absent. Other example: Saccoglossus.

question: Kawas Thermal Power Station is located in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Kawas Thermal Power Station" (Kawas Gas Power Plant) is located near Surat in the state of "Gujarat". (कावास ताप विद्युत संयंत्र — गुजरात)

• It is a gas-based thermal power plant owned and operated by the NTPC Limited, drawing gas from the Hazira–Bijaipur–Jagdishpur (HBJ) pipeline.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other important power plants in Gujarat: Ukai, Wanakbori, Sikka, Dhuvaran, Gandhinagar (thermal), Kakrapar (nuclear) and Charanka Solar Park.

• NTPC Limited, founded in 1975, is India's largest power utility and a Maharatna company.

NOTE

• India's power mix relies heavily on thermal (coal and gas) power, which supplies well over half of installed capacity, followed by renewables, hydro and nuclear.

question: Which among the following is a subject of Union Lists in Constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Extradition.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Extradition" (the surrender of a fugitive to another country) is a subject of the "Union List" in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution, because it concerns foreign affairs and relations with other countries. (संघ सूची — प्रत्यर्पण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Liquor (intoxicating liquors)" is a State List subject.

• "Social planning / social and economic planning" and "Boilers" are in the Concurrent List.

• The Seventh Schedule divides powers into three lists: Union List (originally 97 subjects), State List (originally 66) and Concurrent List (originally 47).

NOTE

• Union List examples: defence, foreign affairs, atomic energy, railways, banking, currency, citizenship, extradition.

• State List: police, public health, agriculture, prisons, local government.

• Concurrent List: education, forests, marriage, bankruptcy, criminal law and procedure. In case of a conflict, the Union law prevails (Article 254). Residuary powers rest with the Union (Article 248).

question: The novel 'The Palace of Illusions' is written by __________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Palace of Illusions" (2008) was written by "Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni". It retells the Mahabharata from the point of view of Draupadi (Panchaali). (द पैलेस ऑफ इल्यूजन्स — चित्रा बनर्जी दिवाकरुनी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Indu Sundaresan wrote "The Twentieth Wife" and "The Feast of Roses".

NOTE

• Indian authors and Booker Prizes: Arundhati Roy — The God of Small Things (1997); Aravind Adiga — The White Tiger (2008); Salman Rushdie — Midnight's Children (1981); Geetanjali Shree — Tomb of Sand (International Booker, 2022).

question: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced in 2022 that she will launch the ______ platform, which is an online learning platform for Oriental and South Asian Studies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharat Vidya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 2022, Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced the launch of the "Bharat Vidya" platform — an online learning platform for Oriental and South Asian Studies, an initiative associated with the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (BORI), Pune. (भारत विद्या — ऑनलाइन शिक्षण मंच)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (BORI), founded in 1917 in Pune, is famous for preparing the critical edition of the Mahabharata.

• "Bharat Vidya" (Indology) covers Sanskrit, Prakrit, Pali, manuscripts, epics and the classical heritage of South Asia.

NOTE

• Nirmala Sitharaman became India's first full-time woman Finance Minister in 2019; she has also served as Defence Minister and Commerce & Industry Minister.
